plants.name: Ashwagandha
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional vitality and stress-support formulations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-season, drought-tolerant shrub; sunny position and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally described as a rasayana and restorative herb; clinical effects depend on preparation and are not established by this profile.

plants.name: Aloe Vera
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Topical skin-care preparations, Ornamental succulent. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.

plants.name: Neem

plants.name: Amla

plants.name: Palash
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Natural dye, Traditional preparations, Ornamental tree. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A drought-tolerant tropical tree; full sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Flowers, seeds and gum are used in traditional preparations; flowers also provide natural dye.
parts_commonly_used: Flowers, seeds, gum, bark and leaves

plants.name: Shalmali
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Gum and fibre, Traditional preparations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A large tropical tree; full sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Gum and other parts have traditional uses; the tree is also valued for fibre and habitat.

plants.name: Aralu
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional bark-based preparations, Timber and shade. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A tropical deciduous tree; full sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Bark and leaves appear in traditional preparations; it is also a timber and shade tree.

plants.name: Bakayan
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional external preparations, Botanical pest-control uses. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A deciduous tree; sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Leaves, bark and seeds have traditional and pest-control uses; the seeds are not edible.
plants.note: Seeds and concentrated extracts can be toxic; do not ingest.

plants.name: Raktachandan
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Red dye, Woodcraft and cultural use. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A dry-tropical tree; full sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Heartwood is prized for dye, carving and cultural uses; medicinal claims require source-specific evidence.
plants.note: Threatened by overharvesting; choose legal, traceable sources.

plants.name: Shatavari Wild
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional root-based formulations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-climate climbing plant; partial shade and moist, well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Root is used in traditional formulations; this is a separate species from cultivated Asparagus racemosus.
plants.note: Verify the species: Shatavari and Shatavari Wild are not the same botanical taxon.

plants.name: Kusha
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Ritual and cultural use, Thatching and soil stabilization. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A drought-tolerant grass; full sun and sandy or dry soils.
plants.medicine_properties: Grass is used in cultural and ritual practices and has traditional applications.

plants.name: Ikshu
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Sugar and food production, Traditional beverage. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A tropical crop; long warm growing season, sun and abundant water.

leaf_features.shape: Long linear blades with sharp margins

plants.medicine_properties: Sugarcane is primarily a food crop; traditional use does not make raw juice a treatment.

plants.name: Priyangu
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional aromatic and topical preparations, Ornamental shrub. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-climate shrub; sun to partial shade and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Flowers and other parts appear in traditional perfumed and topical preparations; uses vary by region.

plants.name: Kumari
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Topical skin-care preparations, Ornamental succulent. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A frost-sensitive succulent; bright sun and sharply drained soil, with sparse watering.
plants.medicine_properties: Aloe leaf gel has topical skin-care uses; this listed taxon is Aloe barbadensis, commonly treated as Aloe vera.
plants.note: Do not ingest aloe latex; verify the product and plant part.

plants.name: Karavira
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Ornamental planting only. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A heat-tolerant shrub; full sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Ornamental flowering shrub; all parts contain cardiac glycosides and are highly poisonous.
parts_commonly_used: No part is safe for home medicinal use
plants.note: Highly poisonous if swallowed or burned; keep away from children and pets.

plants.name: Dhatura
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for No home medicinal use recommended. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-climate annual or short-lived shrub; sun and disturbed, well-drained soil.

leaf_features.shape: Large ovate leaves with irregular teeth

plants.medicine_properties: Traditional use is reported, but tropane alkaloids make the plant highly poisonous and unpredictable.
parts_commonly_used: No part is safe for self-treatment
plants.note: Highly poisonous; can cause delirium, seizures, coma, or death. Do not ingest or handle for remedies.

plants.name: Aak
uses: Traditional external uses only under expert supervision
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional external uses only under expert supervision. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A drought-tolerant tropical shrub; full sun and very well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Latex and other parts are reported in traditional use but are caustic and potentially poisonous.
plants.note: Latex can injure eyes and skin and is toxic if swallowed.

plants.name: Kachnar
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Food preparations from buds/flowers, Traditional formulations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-climate tree; full sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Bark, buds and flowers have traditional uses; flower buds are also eaten in some cuisines.
parts_commonly_used: Bark, flower buds, flowers and leaves

plants.name: Varuna
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional bark-based formulations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A tropical tree, often near water; sun and moist, well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Bark is used in traditional urinary and stone-related formulations; efficacy and safety require clinical assessment.
plants.note: Do not use for urinary or kidney conditions instead of medical evaluation.

plants.name: Rohini
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Traditional bark-based preparations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A tropical deciduous tree; full sun and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Bark is used in traditional formulations; verify identity because vernacular names vary.
plants.note: Check the scientific name; Rohini can refer to different plants.

plants.name: Neem Bark Tree
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Timber, plywood and shade, Not interchangeable with neem. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A fast-growing tropical tree; sun, rainfall and deep well-drained soil.

leaf_features.shape: Large pinnate leaves with toothed leaflets

plants.medicine_properties: A fast-growing timber tree; the supplied name is Neem Bark Tree, but it is Melia dubia, not neem (Azadirachta indica).
plants.note: Different species from true neem; do not transfer neem medicinal claims to this plant.

plants.name: Pomegranate
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Fresh fruit and juice, Traditional food preparations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm, sunny site; tolerates dry periods once established and needs well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Fruit is a food; peel and other parts appear in traditional preparations, but concentrated extracts can interact with medicines.

plants.name: Guava
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Edible fruit, Traditional leaf preparations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-climate fruit tree; full sun, regular water and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Fruit and leaves are used as food; leaves appear in traditional preparations for digestive comfort.

plants.name: Lemon
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Food, juice and flavoring, Household uses. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A frost-sensitive citrus tree; full sun, regular water and well-drained soil.

leaf_features.shape: Oval leaves, often with winged petioles

plants.medicine_properties: Fruit is a food and flavoring; traditional uses do not replace treatment for illness.

plants.name: Curry Leaf
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Food seasoning, Traditional culinary preparations. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-climate shrub or small tree; sun to partial shade and well-drained soil.
plants.medicine_properties: Leaves are widely used as a culinary herb and in traditional food preparations.
parts_commonly_used: berries are not commonly used as food

plants.name: Lemongrass
plants.benefits: Traditionally valued for Tea and food flavoring, Aromatic oil. These traditional uses are not proof of treatment effectiveness.
plants.growing: A warm-season grass; full sun, fertile soil and regular moisture.
plants.medicine_properties: Leaves are used for culinary flavor and herbal tea; traditional uses are not medical treatment.

plants.name: Tulsi (Holy Basil)
plants.benefits: Tulsi is a medicinal herb traditionally used in Ayurveda.
plants.growing: Grows well in warm and sunny locations with good drainage.

plants.name: Amruthaballi (Guduchi/Giloy)
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, immunomodulatory and hepatoprotective properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in Ayurveda and other Indian systems for fever, general weakness, digestive complaints and inflammatory conditions.
plants.description: A perennial climbing shrub with succulent stems, heart-shaped leaves and aerial roots. It is commonly known as Guduchi/Giloy.
plants.growing: A climbing shrub; provide support and suitable warm growing conditions.

plants.name: Ashoka
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with astringent, anti-inflammatory and uterine-supportive properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in Ayurveda, particularly in formulations associated with women's reproductive and menstrual health.
plants.description: A medium-sized evergreen tree with dense foliage and clusters of orange-red flowers.
plants.note: The common name Ashoka can refer to more than one plant in medicinal sources; always use the scientific name with this record.
plants.growing: An evergreen tree suited to a warm, tropical climate.

plants.name: Asthma Weed
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with antiasthmatic, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial and antihistaminic activities; research has investigated several of these properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used for cough, bronchitis, asthma and certain digestive complaints in different traditional medicine systems.
plants.description: A small hairy annual herb with branched stems, opposite leaves and milky latex.
plants.growing: An annual herb commonly found in warm conditions.

plants.name: Balloon Vine
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with anti-inflammatory, analgesic and antiallergic properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used for joint pain, rheumatic complaints, skin problems and inflammatory conditions.
plants.description: A delicate climbing herb with divided leaves, small white flowers and distinctive inflated, balloon-like seed capsules.
plants.growing: A climbing herb that benefits from support for its vines.

plants.name: Betel
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with antimicrobial, antioxidant, digestive and anti-inflammatory properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used as betel leaf (paan), and in various traditional preparations for digestive and oral-related purposes.
plants.description: A perennial evergreen climbing vine with glossy, heart-shaped leaves and slender spikes of flowers.
plants.growing: A perennial climbing vine that prefers warm, humid conditions and support.

plants.name: Brahmi
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with cognitive-supportive, antioxidant and neuroprotective properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in Ayurveda for memory, learning, concentration and general nervous-system support.
plants.description: A small creeping, succulent herb commonly found in wet or marshy areas. It has small fleshy leaves and delicate white flowers.
plants.growing: A creeping herb that commonly grows in wet or marshy areas.

plants.name: Bringaraja (Bhringraj)
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with hepatoprotective, anti-inflammatory, antioxidant and hair-care-related properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in Ayurveda for hair care and in preparations associated with liver and skin health.
plants.description: A small annual herb that can grow erect or prostrate, with opposite leaves and small white flower heads. It commonly grows in moist areas and fields.
plants.growing: An annual herb commonly found in moist areas and fields.

plants.name: Caricature Plant
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with anti-inflammatory and analgesic properties.
plants.benefits: Reported in some Southeast Asian medicinal practices for inflammatory and other ailments.
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with large, attractive leaves that may have purple, green or variegated patterns. It is also widely grown as an ornamental plant.
plants.growing: An evergreen shrub also widely grown as an ornamental plant.

plants.name: Catharanthus (Madagascar Periwinkle)
plants.medicine_properties: Contains important alkaloids, including vincristine and vinblastine, which have established pharmaceutical importance in cancer treatment.
plants.benefits: Used in various folk-medicine practices. Compounds derived from this plant are used in modern anticancer medicines; it is not a self-treatment for cancer.
plants.description: A small evergreen herb or shrub with glossy opposite leaves and characteristic pink, purple or white flowers.
plants.growing: A small evergreen herb or shrub.

plants.name: Drumstick (Moringa)
plants.medicine_properties: Associated with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and nutritional properties; various plant parts have been investigated pharmacologically.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used as a food and in traditional medicine for nutritional support and various common ailments.
plants.description: A fast-growing small-to-medium tree with compound leaves, fragrant flowers and long slender seed pods commonly called drumsticks.
plants.growing: A fast-growing small-to-medium tree.

plants.name: Insulin Plant
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated particularly with blood-glucose-lowering and antidiabetic potential.
uses: Leaves traditionally consumed in herbal preparations associated with diabetes management
plants.benefits: In India, the leaves have traditionally been consumed in herbal preparations associated with diabetes management. This should not replace prescribed diabetes care.
plants.description: A perennial ornamental herb with spirally arranged leaves and reddish-orange flowers. It is also known as fiery costus and spiral flag.
plants.growing: A perennial ornamental herb.

plants.name: Kamakasturi
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with antioxidant, antimicrobial, digestive and anti-inflammatory properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used as an aromatic herb and in preparations for digestive, respiratory and general wellness purposes.
plants.description: An aromatic annual herb with soft green leaves, square stems and small flowers arranged in spikes.
plants.growing: An aromatic annual herb.
plants.note: Kew's medicinal-plant database associates the name Kamakasturi with Ocimum basilicum.

plants.name: Kohlrabi
plants.medicine_properties: Nutritional rather than primarily medicinal; provides vitamin C, dietary fiber and various phytochemicals.
plants.benefits: Mainly consumed as a vegetable; the swollen stem and leaves are used as food.
plants.description: A cool-season vegetable belonging to the cabbage family. Its characteristic edible swollen stem develops above the ground.
plants.growing: A cool-season cultivated vegetable.
plants.note: No specific part is traditionally established as a medicinal drug. Kohlrabi is a cultivated vegetable, not normally classified as a major medicinal plant.

plants.name: Malabar Nut
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with expectorant, bronchodilatory, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used for cough, bronchitis, asthma and other respiratory complaints in Ayurvedic and folk medicine.
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with lance-shaped leaves and white flowers marked with purple or red streaks.
plants.growing: An evergreen shrub.

plants.name: Nelavembu
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antimicrobial and hepatoprotective properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in Ayurveda and Siddha medicine for fever, digestive complaints and various inflammatory conditions.
plants.description: A small annual herb with an erect, branched stem, narrow lance-shaped leaves and small white flowers with purple markings.
plants.growing: A small annual herb.

plants.name: Arive Dantu (Green Amaranth)
plants.medicine_properties: Primarily a leafy food plant; leaves provide dietary nutrients and are traditionally used as greens.
plants.benefits: The tender leaves and shoots are cooked and eaten as a leafy vegetable.
plants.description: An annual herb with green, oval leaves and small green flowers arranged in slender clusters.
plants.growing: A fast-growing annual herb that grows well in warm conditions.

plants.name: Globe Amaranth
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; research findings do not establish it as a treatment.
plants.benefits: Best known as an ornamental plant; its flowers are also used in some traditional herbal preparations.
plants.description: An annual herb with papery, globe-shaped flower heads, commonly magenta, purple, pink or white.
plants.growing: A heat-tolerant annual that grows best in sunny locations with well-drained soil.

plants.name: Hibiscus (China Rose)
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with antioxidant and hair-care properties; evidence and uses vary by preparation.
plants.benefits: Widely grown as an ornamental shrub; flowers and leaves are used in some traditional hair-care and herbal preparations.
plants.description: An evergreen shrub with glossy, toothed leaves and large, showy flowers with a prominent central column of stamens.
plants.growing: A tropical shrub that prefers warmth, sunlight and moist, well-drained soil.

plants.name: Koranda (Karonda)
plants.medicine_properties: The fruits are mainly valued as food; traditional medicinal uses are reported but should not be considered proven treatments.
plants.benefits: Its sour fruits are commonly used in pickles, chutneys and other cooked preparations.
plants.description: A thorny evergreen shrub with opposite leaves, fragrant white flowers and small fruits that ripen from green to red or dark purple.
plants.growing: A hardy shrub suited to warm climates and well-drained soil.

plants.name: Malabar Spinach
plants.medicine_properties: Primarily a nutritious leafy vegetable; it is not a substitute for medical treatment.
plants.benefits: The fleshy leaves and tender stems are cooked and eaten as a leafy vegetable in warm-climate cuisines.
plants.description: A fast-growing climbing vine with thick, glossy, heart-shaped leaves and small flowers followed by dark berries.
plants.growing: A warm-season vine that grows well with support and regular moisture.

plants.name: Mint
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with digestive and aromatic properties; specific effects vary by preparation.
plants.benefits: The aromatic leaves are widely used to flavor foods and drinks and in traditional preparations for digestive comfort.
plants.description: An aromatic perennial herb with square stems, opposite toothed leaves and small flowers arranged in spikes.
plants.growing: A spreading herb that grows well in moist soil and partial to full sunlight.
plants.note: Mint is a broad common name; this entry represents spearmint (Mentha spicata).

plants.name: Padri (Fragrant Padri Tree)
plants.medicine_properties: Traditional medicinal use is reported for different plant parts; clinical effectiveness is not established.
plants.benefits: A native tree valued for its fragrant flowers and reported use in traditional herbal practices.
plants.description: A deciduous tree with compound leaves, fragrant pale yellow flowers often marked with purple, and long narrow capsules.
plants.growing: A deciduous tree suited to warm climates and seasonally moist conditions.
plants.note: The common name Padri may refer to different plants regionally; this record uses Stereospermum chelonoides.

plants.name: Nooni (Noni)
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with antioxidant, anti-inflammatory and antimicrobial properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in South and Southeast Asian and Pacific medicine practices for digestive, inflammatory and general wellness purposes.
plants.description: A small evergreen tree or shrub with large glossy leaves, white tubular flowers and distinctive irregularly shaped greenish-white fruits.
plants.growing: A small evergreen tree or shrub.

plants.name: Parijatha (Night-flowering Jasmine)
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, antipyretic and antimicrobial properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in Ayurveda and folk medicine for fever, joint-related complaints, digestive problems and various inflammatory conditions.
plants.description: A small tree or shrub with rough leaves and highly fragrant white flowers with orange-red centers. The flowers open at night and usually fall by morning.
plants.growing: A small tree or shrub.

plants.name: Thumbe (Thumbai)
plants.medicine_properties: Traditionally associated with anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antioxidant and insect-repellent properties.
plants.benefits: Traditionally used in Indian folk medicine for cough, cold, fever, skin-related complaints and insect bites.
plants.description: A small aromatic herb with an erect, hairy stem, opposite leaves and distinctive white flowers arranged in clusters around the stem.
plants.growing: A small aromatic herb.
